article_content: Sean Manning is the CEO and Founder of Payroll Vault Franchising LLC, a CPA, and a thought leader in the financial field. A well-known proverb states that the best way to eat an elephant is ‘one bite at a time.’ This saying highlights a valuable lesson: tackling large jobs, challenges, or problems is best done slowly, steadily, and in stages. As the co-founder of a payroll service franchise, I recognize the wisdom in applying this lesson to business—especially when business owners consider their plans and goals for 2024. Planning for the upcoming year is a standard business practice for many organizations. However, it can seem overwhelming, particularly for small-business owners, when viewed in its entirety. Therefore, my advice to entrepreneurs contemplating 2024 is to proceed one step at a time. Looking Ahead: From my observations, the economy in 2024 is likely to experience slower growth and could potentially enter a recession. According to a report from The Conference Board, a global nonprofit think tank, economists predict that the United States' gross domestic product (GDP) growth will slow from 2.2% in 2023 to 0.8% in 2024. The average personal consumption expenditure (PCE) inflation for 2024 is forecast at 2.4%—lower than most of 2023 but still above the federal target of 2%. Interest rates are also rising; as of September, the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained a target interest rate of 5.25% to 5.5%, the highest rate in over 20 years. This situation is causing many businesses to cut spending. Labor access also presents a challenge. An October report from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce indicates that hiring has exceeded resignations since November 2020, with recent data showing 9.6 million job openings but only 6.4 million unemployed workers in the U.S. Entering 2024, the lodging, travel, and food service industries may face reduced demand, as financial inflation makes price increases necessary. However, personal and business services are positioned for more opportunities and growth. The Goal-Setting Process: Given the uncertain economic outlook for 2024, business owners should plan to optimize the year. Drawing from my experience as a business owner and financial industry member, I recommend pursuing small-scale, achievable goals for 2024. The economic uncertainty in 2024 suggests that pursuing far-reaching, high-stakes business goals requiring substantial investments of time, money, and effort is risky, so I advise against it. Some risk is inevitable for progress. However, for 2024, I recommend that business owners take only calculated risks, ones they can afford to lose in the short term if unmet. When setting any goals, business owners should perform thorough due diligence. They should document their goals and plans, communicate with staff and partners, and actively manage progress with relatable projects that validate their efforts. I recommend starting with an end-of-year meeting in 2023 with staff and partners to review historical business data and determine reasonable annual achievements. Setting one or two long-term annual goals, divided into smaller quarterly projects supported by weekly or monthly action items, is also beneficial. New business owners may lack the experience to confidently assess achievable annual targets. In such cases, consider hiring a consultant, advisor, or mentor to assist with goal-setting and management. The next step involves delegating smaller projects within the long-term goals for 2024. Evaluate individual employee capabilities and create teams to work on short-term projects. A well-managed team should handle two to three of these projects concurrently. Finally, business owners should maintain open communication with their staff, checking in at least monthly, if not weekly, to ensure smooth progress. Measurable progress should be evident within three to six months. Business owners should address problems by reassigning staff, securing additional funds or resources, or adjusting milestones and expectations. As the year-end approaches, business owners naturally start planning ahead. Planning for a full year can be daunting due to unpredictable events. However, they should avoid becoming overwhelmed into indecision or inaction. Multitasking is stressful and counterproductive. Business owners should collaborate with staff and partners, break down large tasks, delegate to qualified individuals, and communicate effectively to ensure smooth operations. In essence, they should plan for 2024 as one would eat an elephant: one bite at a time. Forbes Business Council is the foremost growth and networking organization for business owners and leaders. article_content: LeBron James, formerly of the Miami Heat, announced in July his return to the Cleveland Cavaliers in Ohio. Consequently, he is selling his luxurious Florida mansion. As LeBron James relocates from South Florida, his Coconut Grove mansion is being listed for $17 million. He is moving back to his residence near Akron, Ohio, a 35,440 square-foot property acquired in 2003 for $2.1 million.  The opulent Florida mansion, spanning 12,178 square feet, features six bedrooms, eight bathrooms, an infinity pool, and docks accommodating two 60-foot yachts, according to The Bleacher Report. Homecoming: LeBron James of the Miami Heat is returning to his native Ohio to pursue a championship for the Cleveland Cavaliers, selling his Florida mansion in the process. Entertainment Ready: The 12,178 square-foot home is illuminated at night and provides ample accommodation in its six bedrooms. Pristine Appeal: The home's bright white exterior, once appealing to LeBron James, could attract buyers willing to invest $17 million. Endless Luxury: The infinity pool creates a seamless visual experience within the 12,178 square-foot property. Fit for a Star: LeBron's residence includes a private movie theater, perfect for enjoying films, especially for the future homeowner. Wine Connoisseur's Dream: The wine cellar is ideal for wine enthusiasts, provided they can afford the substantial price of the home. Luxury Living: Prospective buyers of this $17 million home will need significant financial resources. NBC reports the mansion includes a movie theater, guest house, office, chef's kitchen, three-car garage, waterfront pool and deck, and a sizable wine cellar. Interested buyers should contact Tomi Rose of Opulence International Realty. The listing agent, Tomi Rose, understands the needs of professional athletes, being engaged to former Miami Heat player Mark Strickland. Regarding his move, LeBron stated his unbreakable bond with Ohio and his desire to bring a championship to the state. He told Sports Illustrated, 'Before anyone ever cared where I would play basketball, I was a kid from Northeast Ohio. It's where I walked. It's where I ran. It's where I cried. It's where I bled. It holds a special place in my heart. People there have seen me grow up. I sometimes feel like I'm their son. Their passion can be overwhelming. But it drives me.' He explained that while his initial move to Florida was to win championships, he now aims to elevate Cleveland's status. 'My goal is still to win as many titles as possible, no question. But what's most important for me is bringing one trophy back to Northeast Ohio,' he told Sports Illustrated. LeBron is returning to Ohio but not taking the $17 million mansion. He will reside in a similarly lavish 35,440-square-foot home in Bath Township near Akron, Ohio, which he purchased in 2003 for $2.1 million. Luxurious Bathing: This bathroom exemplifies the luxury awaiting those who can afford the $17 million price tag. Sunshine Views: For $17 million, enjoy waking up to stunning views from your new home. Convenient Laundry: The in-house laundry facilities ensure clean attire after workouts or nights out. Paradise Found: This home, with all its luxuries, is perfect for athletes, celebrities, or anyone seeking opulence. LeBron's Ohio Residence: Life is comfortable when transitioning from one mansion to another, especially when the new one is larger and less expensive.

article_content: By The Associated Press The number of suicides across the military decreased by more than 15 percent in 2013, despite an increase among Army National Guard and Reserve soldiers compared to the previous year. According to data gathered by The Associated Press from major military branches, 151 active-duty soldiers died by suicide in 2013. That's 24 fewer than the 185 suicides in 2012. However, 152 members of the Army National Guard and Reserve took their own lives last year, compared to 140 the previous year. Col. Elspeth Ritchie, from the Office of the Army Surgeon General, discussed efforts to study and understand suicide among American soldiers who served in Iraq and Afghanistan. The Pentagon planned to release a report on military suicides on Friday, April 25, 2014, with preliminary figures showing a drop in rates for 2013. There were 289 active-duty suicides across all major military branches in 2013, down from 343 in 2012. This decrease in overall suicides may be a promising sign for the Pentagon, which has been actively increasing prevention efforts to help those at risk. According to the Pentagon report, almost 93 percent of military suicides were male, 74 percent were white, and nearly 40 percent were between 17 and 24 years old. Approximately 65 percent used a firearm; about 76 percent of those used a privately owned gun, while 25 percent died by asphyxiation, including hanging. More than 33 percent tested positive for alcohol use, and about 24 percent tested positive for drugs. Military leaders are hesitant to declare the slight decrease a victory. 'I think we've changed the cultural mindset — that it's okay for a sailor, soldier, airman, or Marine to come forward and ask for help,' said Navy Rear Adm. Sean Buck, who oversees suicide prevention for his branch. 'We're trying to reduce the stigma that used to exist.' While many reservists who committed suicide served in Afghanistan in 2013, there is no conclusive evidence linking overseas service to suicide. The AP reported that many reservists who committed suicide served in Iraq and Afghanistan, but there's no evident link between service and suicide. Also featured in the report: — 55 percent of unsuccessful suicide attempts involved drugs. — 42 percent had a history of behavioral health diagnoses. — More than 28 percent had talked about harming themselves prior to the suicide. — 40 percent reported family or relationship stress in the 90 days prior to suicide; 32 percent reported financial or work stress. — 57 percent had been deployed. — 47 percent had been deployed to the Iraq or Afghanistan wars.

article_content: Transform your wardrobe without sewing! This guide provides easy DIY projects to revamp your clothes using simple tools and techniques. Inspired by celebrity styles, these no-sew updates, created by InStyle's Jenni Radosevich (ispy-diy.com), are quick and fun. Check out the projects below: Lacy T-Shirt: Inspired by Mena Suvari What You'll Need: Long-sleeve cotton T-shirt, Unique Stitch glue, 1 yard of 6-inch-wide lace trim, scissors. How-To: 1. Lay lace trim across the T-shirt's width, about 2 inches from the bottom. Cut the lace to align with the shirt's side seams. 2. Dot glue on the back of the lace and position it on the shirt. 3. Secure the lace by applying a thin glue line around its entire edge. 4. Repeat with a second strip, about 2 inches above the first. 5. Let dry for 24 hours. (Hand wash.) Feather-Collared LBD: Inspired by Julianne Moore What You'll Need: 1 foot of feather trim, Multi-Grip glue, 1 yard of black satin ribbon, black dress, scissors. How-To: 1. Cut 15 1-inch and 2 1-foot ribbon pieces. 2. Shape the feather trim into a 'U' to fit correctly around the neck. 3. Glue 1-inch ribbon pieces (folded in half lengthwise) over the feather trim around the 'U', overlapping them to create a curve. 4. Glue 1-foot-long ribbons to both ends. 5. Let dry for 24 hours. Tie around the neck over the dress. Fringed Clutch: Inspired by Joy Bryant What You'll Need: Sticky Back Velcro tape, 1-foot leather fringe, flap clutch, scissors. How-To: 1. Cut the fringe trim and Sticky Back Velcro tape to the length of the clutch flap. 2. Remove the backing from one side of the Velcro and stick it to the inside of the clutch's flap. 3. Remove the backing from the other side of the Velcro and adhere it to the fringe. Ribbon Necklace: Inspired by Emily Blunt What You'll Need: 1½ feet of satin ribbon, jeweled or chain choker-length necklace, scissors. How-To: 1. Open the necklace and knot the ribbon to one end. Decide on the desired length and cut off any excess ribbon. 2. Tie the other end of the ribbon to the necklace. Jewel-Lined Pencil Skirt: Inspired by Paula Patton What You'll Need: Pencil skirt, iron, Heat 'n Bond Ultra Hold iron-on adhesive (¼" x 10 yards), 1 yard of beaded trim, scissors. How-To: 1. Preheat the iron to the silk setting. Place Heat 'n Bond on the back of the beaded trim. Lightly glide the iron across the paper side for 1-2 seconds. 2. Allow to cool, then peel off the paper backing. 3. Place the trim right side up on the bottom edge of the skirt; iron the inside of the skirt for 5 seconds. 4. Cut the trim flush with the slit in the back of the skirt. (Dry-clean.) Studded Shirt: Inspired by Natalie Portman What You'll Need: 2 feet of studded trim, white button-down ¾-sleeve shirt, Unique Stitch glue, scissors. How-To: 1. Starting with the sleeves, cut 2 pieces of studded trim to cover the circumference of each cuff (avoid covering the buttons). 2. Apply a thin glue layer to the trim and position it on the left cuff. Repeat on the right cuff. 3. Cut 2 pieces of trim to cover the front of each side of the collar. 4. Apply a thin glue layer to the trim pieces and position them on the collar. 5. Let dry for 24 hours. (Hand wash.)
translated_content: Proměňte svůj šatník bez šití! Tato příručka nabízí snadné DIY projekty pro vylepšení vašeho oblečení pomocí jednoduchých nástrojů a technik. Inspirováno stylem celebrit, tyto rychlé úpravy bez šití, vytvořené Jenni Radosevich z InStyle (ispy-diy.com), jsou zábavné a snadné. Prohlédněte si následující projekty: Tričko s krajkou: Inspirováno Menou Suvari Co budete potřebovat: Bavlněné tričko s dlouhým rukávem, lepidlo Unique Stitch, 1 metr 15 cm široké krajky, nůžky. Postup: 1. Položte krajku přes šířku trička, asi 5 cm od spodního okraje. Ustřihněte krajku tak, aby odpovídala bočním švům trička. 2. Naneste tečky lepidla na zadní stranu krajky a přiložte ji na tričko. 3. Zajistěte krajku nanesením tenké vrstvy lepidla po celém obvodu okraje krajky. 4. Opakujte s druhým pruhem, asi 5 cm nad prvním. 5. Nechte 24 hodin zaschnout. (Ruční praní.) Malé černé s peřím na límci: Inspirováno Julianne Moore Co budete potřebovat: 30 cm peříčkové stuhy, lepidlo Multi-Grip, 1 metr černé saténové stuhy, černé šaty, nůžky. Postup: 1. Nastříhejte 15 krátkých proužků (2,5 cm) a 2 dlouhé proužky stuhy (30 cm). 2. Vytvarujte peříčkovou stuhu do tvaru 'U', aby správně seděla kolem krku. 3. Lepte krátké kousky stuhy (přeložené napůl) přes peříčkovou stuhu kolem 'U', překrývejte je, abyste vytvořili křivku. 4. Přilepte dlouhé stuhy na oba konce. 5. Nechte 24 hodin zaschnout. Uvažte kolem krku přes šaty. Kabelka s třásněmi: Inspirováno Joy Bryant Co budete potřebovat: Lepicí suchý zip, 30 cm kožených třásní, kabelka s klopou, nůžky. Postup: 1. Ustřihněte třásně a suchý zip na délku klopy kabelky. 2. Odstraňte krycí vrstvu z jedné strany suchého zipu a přilepte jej na vnitřní stranu klopy kabelky. 3. Odstraňte krycí vrstvu z druhé strany suchého zipu a přilepte jej na třásně. Náhrdelník se stuhou: Inspirováno Emily Blunt Co budete potřebovat: 45 cm saténové stuhy, náhrdelník (řetízek nebo s kameny) délky chokeru, nůžky. Postup: 1. Otevřete náhrdelník a uvažte stuhu na jeden konec. Rozhodněte se, jak dlouhý chcete náhrdelník mít, a odstřihněte přebytečnou stuhu. 2. Uvažte druhý konec stuhy k náhrdelníku. Pouzdrová sukně s ozdobami: Inspirováno Paulou Patton Co budete potřebovat: Pouzdrová sukně, žehlička, tavná lepicí páska Heat 'n Bond Ultra Hold (6 mm x 9 metrů), 1 metr ozdobné stuhy s korálky, nůžky. Postup: 1. Předehřejte žehličku na stupeň pro hedvábí. Umístěte Heat 'n Bond na zadní stranu ozdobné stuhy s korálky. Lehce přejeďte žehličkou po papírové straně po dobu 1-2 sekund. 2. Nechte vychladnout a poté odstraňte papírovou vrstvu. 3. Umístěte stuhu lícem nahoru na spodní okraj sukně; zažehlete zevnitř sukně po dobu 5 sekund. 4. Zarovnejte stuhu s rozparkem na zadní straně sukně a ustřihněte. (Doporučuje se chemické čištění.) Košile s cvočky: Inspirováno Natalie Portman Co budete potřebovat: 60 cm stuhy s cvočky, bílá košile s ¾ rukávy, lepidlo Unique Stitch, nůžky. Postup: 1. Začněte rukávy: ustřihněte 2 kusy stuhy s cvočky, které obepnou každou manžetu (vyhněte se knoflíkům). 2. Naneste tenkou vrstvu lepidla na stuhu a přilepte ji na levou manžetu. Opakujte na pravé manžetě. 3. Ustřihněte 2 kusy stuhy, které zakryjí přední strany límce. 4. Naneste tenkou vrstvu lepidla na stuhy a přilepte je na límec. 5. Nechte 24 hodin zaschnout. (Ruční praní.)

article_content: Small pieces of metal were discovered 'strategically placed' on play equipment and the ground in a children's playground. Approximately 20 metal pieces, appearing to be cut from a drink can, were found scattered throughout the playground at Kensington Park in Sydney's east on Tuesday. Jenny Rose found the shards when she took her 14-month-old grandson, Archie, to the park. The shards were hidden and only visible when they reflected sunlight. Alice Rose, Archie's mother, told Daily Mail Australia, 'My son went to climb the stairs, and my mum and other parents noticed shiny objects.' 'It looked like a cut-up soft drink can. The pieces were placed on the steps and play equipment, with some wedged into the rubber flooring.' 'It definitely wasn't an accident... she and other parents searched the area and removed the metal from the ground.' Ms. Rose stated that she takes her son to the park daily and was shocked that someone intentionally placed metal pieces where children could be hurt. 'He was going down the slide, and the metal was there, where children place their hands. They could have easily scratched themselves going down,' she said. 'Many small children play in that area. It could have caused serious harm.' Alice Rose's 14-month-old son, Archie, was at Kensington Park playground when the metal shards were discovered on the stairs, embedded in the rubber matting, and on the slide. Ms. Rose's mother and other parents found 20 metal pieces after searching the playground for 30 minutes on Tuesday. 'It's frightening that someone consciously planned this,' Ms. Rose said. 'We go there every day. There are some strange people out there; who would do that?' 'Seeing the metal pieces reminds other parents to be vigilant.' The metal shards, found by Jenny Rose, were concealed and only noticeable when reflecting sunlight. Randwick City Council dispatched three teams on Wednesday to inspect Kensington Park and two nearby parks. Randwick Mayor Ted Seng said, 'I was very concerned to learn of this incident, and we appreciate the local residents bringing it to our attention.' 'Council sent outdoor crews to Kensington Park and adjacent parks to inspect and thoroughly check the area. Fortunately, no further evidence of shredded cans was found.' 'This is the first instance of this happening at a Randwick City playground that I am aware of, and I hope it is the last. We have notified local police about this incident.' The incident came to light after Ms. Rose posted photos of the metal shards on a Facebook group to warn other mothers. 'Today, we found these in the playground at Kensington Park, strategically spread across the ground and on the play equipment,' she wrote. 'They are small, sharp pieces of metal, cut and bent with the intent of hurting innocent children. Please check the play area before your little one plays; there are some disturbed individuals out there.' Her post sparked outrage from other mothers who reported similar incidents in nearby parks at Bronte and Queens Park in recent months. Police were unaware of any reports of metal shards intentionally left in playgrounds when Daily Mail Australia contacted them on Wednesday.

Jenny Rose našla střepy, když vzala svého 14měsíčního vnuka Archieho do parku. Střepy byly skryté a viditelné pouze, když se na nich odráželo slunce. Alice Roseová, Archieho matka, řekla Daily Mail Australia: 'Můj syn chtěl vylézt po schodech a moje máma a další rodiče si všimli lesklých věcí.' 'Vypadalo to jako rozřezaná plechovka od limonády. Kousky byly umístěné na schodech a herních prvcích, a některé byly zaklíněné v gumové podlaze.' 'Určitě to nebyla nehoda... máma a další rodiče prohledali okolí a posbírali kov ze země.' Paní Roseová řekla, že bere svého syna do parku každý den a byla šokovaná, že někdo úmyslně rozmístil kovové kousky tam, kde by se děti mohly zranit. 'Šel dolů po klouzačce a kov byl tam, kde si děti dávají ruce. Mohly se snadno poškrábat,' řekla. 'V téhle oblasti si hraje hodně malých dětí. Mohlo to způsobit vážné zranění.' Čtrnáctiměsíční Archie, syn Alice Roseové, byl na hřišti v Kensington Parku, když tam našli kovové střepy na schodech, v gumové podložce a na klouzačce. Matka paní Roseové a další rodiče našli 20 kousků kovu poté, co v úterý 30 minut prohledávali hřiště. 'Je děsivé, že to někdo vědomě naplánoval,' řekla paní Roseová. 'Chodíme tam každý den. Jsou mezi námi divní lidé; kdo by to udělal?' 'Když vidím ty kovové kousky, připomíná mi to, že musíme být ostražití.' Kovové střepy, které našla Jenny Roseová, byly skryté a viditelné pouze, když se na nich odráželo slunce. Rada města Randwick vyslala ve středu tři hlídky, aby zkontrolovaly Kensington Park a dva okolní parky. Starosta Randwicku Ted Seng řekl: 'Byl jsem velmi znepokojen, když jsem se o tom dozvěděl, a vážíme si toho, že nás místní obyvatelé na to upozornili.' 'Rada vyslala do Kensington Parku a přilehlých parků pracovníky, aby prohledali a důkladně zkontrolovali okolí. Naštěstí nenašli žádné další střepy z plechovek.' 'Je to poprvé, co se něco takového stalo na hřišti v Randwicku, a doufám, že naposledy. Informovali jsme místní policii.' Incident se dostal na světlo poté, co paní Roseová zveřejnila fotografie kovových střepů ve facebookové skupině a varovala tak ostatní matky. 'Dnes jsme je našli na hřišti v Kensington Parku, strategicky rozmístěné po zemi a na herních prvcích,' napsala. 'Jsou to malé ostré kousky kovu, nařezané a ohnuté tak, aby zranily nevinné děti. Prosím, zkontrolujte hřiště, než si na něm vaše dítě začne hrát; mezi námi chodí narušení jedinci.' Její příspěvek vyvolal pobouření mezi ostatními matkami, které nahlásily podobné incidenty v parcích Bronte a Queens Park v posledních měsících. Policie neměla žádné zprávy o úmyslně ponechaných kovových střepů na hřištích, když je Daily Mail Australia ve středu kontaktoval.

article_content: A major US government report released recently suggests that the global middle class is set to surge, potentially tripling in size within the next two decades. By 2030, China and India are projected to eclipse the US and EU in global influence, according to the study. This boom in middle-income individuals could place immense strain on resources like food and water, the report cautions. The report, issued by the National Intelligence Council, indicates that economic growth in China, India, and Brazil will fuel this middle-class expansion, fostering enhanced education, improved healthcare, and greater empowerment for women. A significant portion of this emerging middle class is expected to reside in urban areas, with approximately two-thirds of the global population living in cities by 2030. Technology is seen as a possible remedy to mitigate these challenges, potentially boosting economic productivity despite population growth, rapid urbanization, and climate change. However, the study also outlines potential worst-case scenarios, including conflict over scarce resources and global economic instability. Extraordinary events, such as severe pandemics or accelerated climate change, are identified as 'Black Swans' that could dramatically reshape the future. On a positive note, the U.S. has the potential to achieve energy independence thanks to shale gas reserves, the report notes.

Podle studie se očekává, že do roku 2030 Čína a Indie zastíní USA a EU v globálním vlivu. Tento boom u jednotlivců se středními příjmy by mohl podle zprávy enormně zatížit zdroje, jako jsou potraviny a voda. Zpráva, kterou vydala Národní zpravodajská rada, naznačuje, že hospodářský růst v Číně, Indii a Brazílii podpoří tuto expanzi střední třídy, podpoří lepší vzdělání, zlepšení zdravotní péče a větší posílení postavení žen. Očekává se, že značná část této nově vznikající střední třídy bude sídlit v městských oblastech, přičemž přibližně dvě třetiny světové populace budou do roku 2030 žít ve městech. Technologie je považována za možný lék ke zmírnění těchto výzev, potenciálně zvyšuje hospodářskou produktivitu navzdory růstu populace, rychlé urbanizaci a změně klimatu. Studie však také nastiňuje potenciální nejhorší scénáře, včetně konfliktů o vzácné zdroje a globální hospodářské nestability. Mimořádné události, jako jsou závažné pandemie nebo zrychlené změny klimatu, jsou identifikovány jako 'černé labutě', které by mohly dramaticky přetvořit budoucnost. Pozitivní je, že USA mají potenciál dosáhnout energetické nezávislosti díky zásobám břidlicového plynu, uvádí zpráva.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter PUBLISHED: 16:56 EST, January 14, 2013 | UPDATED: 03:31 EST, January 16, 2013 Shock jock Howard Stern on Monday apologized for criticizing 'Girls' star Lena Dunham, after calling her a 'little fat chick' and saying that seeing her naked on the show 'feels like rape.' The controversy began on Stern’s radio show last week, when he described Dunham as 'a little fat girl who kinda looks like Jonah Hill, and she keeps taking her clothes off, and it kind of feels like rape.' Stern said he told his producer to contact Dunham and let her know he wanted to explain and apologize for his comments. Scroll down for video Outspoken: Howard Stern, left, used his radio show to air his views on the show 'Girls' and ridicule the looks of Lena Dunham, right. Fans have criticized the 59-year-old, calling him a 'bully'. 'It makes me feel bad and I think she is getting the impression that I somehow think she’s just a talentless little fat chick,' Stern said. Rude: Stern described Golden Globe winner Lena Dunham as 'the little fat chick who writes the show'. The 59-year-old had earlier criticized 'Girls' for focusing too much on the exploits of Dunham's character, Hannah Horvath. He says he was introduced to the show by his wife, Beth Ostrosky, but has obviously watched enough to become acquainted with the format. 'I learned that this little fat chick writes the show and directs the show, and that makes sense to me because she's such a camera hog that the other characters barely are on,' he said. 'My opinion, if I was a producer on that, I'd say, 'Honey, you're a little too close to the project. You need to allow the other characters to breathe a little and let us get invested in them,' he continued. 'Good for her. It's hard for little fat chicks to get anything going.' Dunham, 26, is also the show's producer, but she said she had no hard feelings towards the America's Got Talent judge. 'I did find out that Howard Stern really hates [Girls]. I'm a Howard Stern fan, and really think he has earned the right to free speech and he should just go for it,' she told David Letterman on the Late Show Thursday. Girls stars Zosia Mamet, Lena Dunham, and Allison Williams are pictured at the Golden Globe Awards show. 'But he did say something that is so funny that I wanna get it on my gravestone: 'Congrats to her (Dunham). It's so hard for little fat chicks to get anything going these days',' she said, 'I want my gravestone to say, 'she was a little fat chick and she got it going'.'  Letterman then joked: 'I think that's the essence of life's struggle, isn't it? Before you go to bed tonight, before your head hits the pillow, please consider little fat chicks and how hard it is to get things going.' Although she clearly doesn't need any back-up, fans of the show have since turned on Stern, branding him a bully. Hit: The award-winning series 'Girls' returns to HBO. Howard Stern has criticized it, but his comments were laughed off by Dunham. Several also pointed out he isn't male model material himself. One woman wrote on Twitter: 'Howard Stern talking about not liking 'little fat chicks' on TV is bizarre, since he has a face only radio could love.' Celebrity trainer Tracy Anderson told Us Weekly: 'He’s literally desensitized himself so much over the years. That guy doesn’t know what’s sexy. What is sexy is the way that Lena exposes herself, exposes her soul, wears her heart on her sleeves, and is so freaking confident — that’s sexy.' Others said his comments were 'hilarious' and that he was a 'legend' for commenting on the popular program. The second season of 'Girls' premiered Monday, January 13th. New York stories: The new season of 'Girls' premiered in the US.

article_content: IKEA has triggered a Christmas price war by offering six-foot Christmas trees for just £25, including a £20 money-off voucher. This deal, effectively reducing the price to £5 per tree, threatens to take significant business from garden centers, which typically charge between £40 and £50. It also poses a challenge to British growers, who recently delivered the traditional Christmas tree to Downing Street for the holiday season. IKEA is offering thousands of Nordmann Fir trees sourced from Denmark and Scotland as part of this loss-leader promotion, aimed at boosting sales before Christmas and during its New Year sale. The promotion is expected to create long queues at IKEA stores, which are often congested. This initiative could reverse the recent decline in demand for real trees, as people have been switching to artificial alternatives or designer options, like the paper tree from John Lewis. Research commissioned by the Swedish retailer suggests that British families spend £150 million annually on real Christmas trees. The research found the average price for a six-foot tree with non-drop needles is £48, but families in some areas pay as much as £79.99. The city with the highest average price was Southampton at £60, followed by Birmingham at £56, Warrington at £54, and London and Thurrock, both at £52. The lowest average price was in Leeds at £40, ahead of Nottingham at £41, Manchester at £43, Cardiff at £44, and Glasgow at £44. Previously, IKEA allowed other companies to sell trees in its parking lots. However, after offering its own discounted trees last year, the chain experienced a surplus and had to practically give them away. In the days leading up to Christmas, £25 trees were sold for £7.50, and customers received a £20 voucher. Using the voucher meant effectively getting a free tree and £12.50 to spend. Birgit Hartelius, deputy country sales manager for IKEA in the UK and Ireland, stated: ‘There’s something really special about having a real tree in the home during the festive season, but over the years we’ve seen prices rise to a level that many people can’t afford.’ This Christmas tree offer excludes IKEA stores in Bristol and Croydon. The £20 voucher is valid from January 20 to February 9.

article_content: U.S. Open champion Novak Djokovic has vowed to win the French Open -- the only major championship he didn't win in 2011 -- and complete a career Grand Slam. The 24-year-old Serb, speaking to CNN after his four-set victory over Spain's Rafael Nadal at Flushing Meadows, believes his current form is strong enough to challenge Nadal's dominance on clay. "It will take a lot of effort. I don't think I need to change anything specific in my game," Djokovic said. "I need to believe in myself. I need to go out there and play my shots. I need to maintain that level. It's not easy. Clay is a slower surface and requires a different approach, and Nadal has won the French Open for many years." "Can anyone break Nadal's dominance? It will be difficult to win against him at that tournament. But I'm confident that I have a better chance than ever next year." Djokovic's U.S. Open victory highlighted what has been a remarkable year. It's his third Grand Slam title of 2011, following wins at Wimbledon and the Australian Open. In total, he has won 10 tournaments, playing 66 matches, and lost only twice this year. "It will be a big challenge to match what I did this year in 2012," he told CNN. "I'm still young and motivated every time I step onto the court. I have a strong will to win, which keeps me going, and I'll try to win as many majors as I can." Reflecting on his near-perfect 2011, Djokovic believes his incredible run has given him an advantage against his main rivals. "It's obviously been the best year of my career," Djokovic told CNN. "I think I've matured as a player on the court, and I have much more self-belief. I'm using the confidence I gained from this year's incredible run. When you win that many matches, you feel more comfortable on the court." "When I play my big rivals, Federer and Nadal, I step onto the court wanting to be aggressive and take my chances. It's been a dream run and a dream year, and I'm enjoying every moment of it." Djokovic also described saving two match points against Federer in the semifinals as a turning point. "It's hard to say I was relaxed at that moment because I was two match points down and close to losing," he recalled. "This is what happens at this level. When you play great champions like Federer and Nadal, they always play their best at the later stages of major events." "They have been so dominant in the last few years. You need to come up with those kinds of shots." "I closed my eyes and hit the ball as hard as I could, and luckily it went in."

Není to snadné. Antuka je pomalejší povrch a vyžaduje jiný přístup, a Nadal vyhrál French Open už mnohokrát." "Může vůbec někdo zlomit Nadalovu dominanci? Mám obrovskou vůli vyhrávat, a to mě žene dopředu. Budu se snažit vyhrát co nejvíce grandslamových titulů." Djokovič vzpomínal na svůj téměř dokonalý rok 2011 a věří, že mu jeho neuvěřitelná série zajistila výhodu proti jeho největším rivalům. Djokovič také popsal moment, kdy v semifinále zachránil dva mečboly proti Federerovi, jako zlomový. "Těžko říct, že jsem byl v tu chvíli v klidu, protože jsem prohrával o dva mečboly a byl jsem blízko prohře," vzpomínal. "Takové věci se na této úrovni stávají. article_content: By Charlotte Griffiths. A poster promoting a satirical play about the Monarchy, 'King Charles III', featuring a gagged Prince Charles, has been censored by London Underground due to concerns it might cause offence. The advert for the critically acclaimed production depicts the Prince with white duct tape covering his mouth, in a punk-style portrait. Despite the poster's display across London since the play's opening nearly three weeks prior, Transport for London (TfL) decided to pixelate Charles’s face. The posters advertising 'King Charles III' at The Almeida Theatre Islington were pixelated by TfL because the image was thought to be potentially offensive. TfL attributed the pixelation to Exterion Media, the company responsible for managing adverts on the Tube network. Reportedly, there was confusion regarding the specific reason for the poster's censorship. TfL stated that Exterion Media advised on the ban, fearing potential offence, but could not specify who might be offended. A TfL spokesman explained: ‘We collaborate with Exterion Media, who manage our Tube network adverts and provide guidance. They may suggest certain content could cause offence. Exterion may have deemed the poster inconsistent with their policy.' 'The decision was made independently of us and appears somewhat overzealous. We will address this with them.’ A Clarence House aide confirmed that Prince Charles, who was photographed during a visit to south-west London last month, was not contacted about the use of his image. Tom Moloney of NB Studio, the poster's design firm, expressed surprise at the censorship. He stated: ‘We were unaware until we submitted the artwork. It was returned with a request for changes based on their feedback. We understand it was due to TfL’s regulations regarding permitted content on their sites.’ The Almeida Theatre in Islington, North London, where Mike Bartlett's sold-out play opened on April 3, continues to display a large, uncensored version of the poster. A theatre spokesman commented: ‘I believe the artwork designers had to pixelate Charles’s face for TfL to approve the posters.’ Last night, Clarence House reiterated that Prince Charles was neither consulted about the use of his image, nor did he request the poster's censorship. The play is set after the Queen’s death and centers on the Prince of Wales as he prepares to ascend to the throne after ‘a lifetime of waiting’. Separately, Prince Charles could be crowned King of an independent Scotland under radical plans supported by SNP leader Alex Salmond. This separate ceremony would effectively establish Scotland as a kingdom in its own right. Additional reporting: William Jaffrey.

article_content: The National Australia Bank (NAB) is receiving backlash for its recent marketing initiative that advises clients to set aside their 'sensible side' and indulge a bit by using their credit cards. This campaign has sparked outrage among numerous customers. NAB has been sending personalized letters, designed to appear handwritten, encouraging individuals to tap into their 'impulsive side'. These letters promote the idea of obtaining a new credit card for a bit of 'retail therapy'. One such letter, sent to a teenager in Queensland named Rebekah, specifically suggests applying for a new credit card due to its perceived low-cost benefits, allowing her to 'enjoy some retail therapy'. Mari-Anna Reiljan-Dillon, a 19-year-old, felt 'insulted' upon receiving her customized letter from NAB. Mari-Anna Reiljan-Dillon responded with a letter detailing her reasons for not needing the low-fee card. Annoyed clients have taken to social media, particularly NAB's Facebook page, to voice their displeasure, describing the campaign as 'condescending and insulting'. A father from Toowoomba, writing to The Chronicle, criticized the bank for targeting his 19-year-old daughter, Rebekah. Ms. Reiljan-Dillon also responded with her own handwritten letter back to the bank, arguing that the marketing strategy trivializes individual financial choices. She emphasized that as a responsible money manager and astute investor, she found the letter insulting, suggesting a lack of respect for her financial intelligence. Other customers, like Mary O'Brien, expressed disappointment with the bank's chosen marketing strategy. The campaign has faced substantial negative feedback on platforms like Facebook. One customer directed her concerns to a high-ranking official within the Australian financial institution. A NAB spokesperson defended the campaign, stating that credit card offers are 'only extended to customers that we expect can manage that credit' and that the letter 'highlights the smart ways to reduce credit card interest'. Mary O'Brien, a 52-year-old with marketing experience and a long-standing NAB customer, described the campaign as 'insulting, condescending and poorly targeted'. She found it offensive that the bank, which she has trusted for over 40 years, would imply she needs a credit card. Ms. O'Brien also pointed out an ethical concern, suggesting the campaign implies everyone struggles with financial management, regardless of their debt status. The exact number of complaints is unknown, but numerous social media posts on NAB's Facebook page detail customer dissatisfaction. According to creditcard.com.au, Australians held a total balance of $45 billion on credit cards with an interest-free period as of February 2014. In her letter, Mari-Anna Reiljan-Dillon mentioned Australia's rising credit card debt. She stated she would decline all future credit card offers from the bank. Customers have criticized NAB, stating the campaign devalues individual money-saving habits.

article_content: President Vladimir Putin's press conferences are unlike those I used to attend in Washington, when I covered the White House. The sheer number of journalists, over 1,200, in the hall requires them to use creative methods to attract President Putin's attention, such as stuffed animals, homemade signs, or custom T-shirts promoting their region or news organization. The conference's length was typical at three and a half hours, although some have been longer. This, Vladimir Putin's tenth such event, occurred at a challenging time. As the Russians say, 'the smell of kerosene was in the air,' indicating a sense of impending crisis. The ruble's value was plummeting, the U.S. and Europe were imposing further sanctions, and Russia faced a potential recession, yet the president avoided labeling it a 'crisis.' Putin appeared composed and self-assured as he entered the hall. Close-up shots of his face were displayed on large screens, capturing every expression and gesture. Putin's primary objective was to reassure citizens that Russia could overcome what he termed an 'unfavorable scenario,' promising improvement within two years, possibly sooner. He offered no direct apology for Russia's economic situation. Instead, Putin merely conceded that the Russian Central Bank and the government could have responded more swiftly to the economic challenges. He attributed Russia's economic difficulties to 'external' factors, claiming that sanctions accounted for only '25 to 30%' of the problems. When a BBC reporter inquired about a 'new' Cold War, Putin leaned forward assertively, stating that Russia was simply protecting its own interests. He noted that Moscow has only two military bases abroad, while the U.S. has bases 'all over the world.' He complained that promises against NATO expansion were broken, with the West now erecting 'virtual walls' around Russia. Putin is skilled at shifting blame. When questioned about alleged reprisals by Chechen authorities against families of suspected terrorists and accusations that Russian government-funded TV channels were inciting hatred, Putin immediately referenced the recently released White House torture report. He argued that the U.S. had 'legalized torture' and even developed methods for it, asking, 'How do you explain that?' Putin elaborated on the image of the Russian 'bear,' asserting that the West seeks to 'chain' and 'de-claw' it, rather than allowing it to exist peacefully. A potentially positive note was Putin's statement that the conflict in eastern Ukraine should be resolved peacefully. He admitted to the presence of Russians in eastern Ukraine, describing them as 'volunteers.' Surprisingly, Putin called on journalists known for their critical stance towards the Kremlin, resulting in some difficult questions. When Putin suggested a 'fine line' between the opposition and a 'Fifth Column'—traitors to Russia—reporters pressed him to name members of the 'Fifth Column,' which he did not do. Others questioned him about the salary of Igor Sechin, head of Rosneft, to which he claimed ignorance. In a notable moment, a Russian reporter asked if Putin feared a 'palace coup' from within his inner circle. Putin, known for his humor, despite his tough image, responded with a smile: 'We can't have a palace coup because we have no palaces.' He stated that stability relies on the support of the Russian people, who 'believe we are acting in their interest.'

Obrovský počet novinářů, více než 1200, v sále vyžaduje, aby používali kreativní metody, jak upoutat pozornost prezidenta Putina, například plyšová zvířátka, ručně vyrobené transparenty nebo trička na zakázku s reklamou na jejich region nebo zpravodajskou organizaci. Délka konference byla obvyklá, tři a půl hodiny, i když některé byly delší. Tato, v pořadí desátá tisková konference Vladimira Putina, se konala v náročné době. Jak říkají Rusové, 've vzduchu byl cítit petrolej,' což naznačuje blížící se krizi. Hodnota rublu strmě klesala, USA a Evropa uvalovaly další sankce a Rusko čelilo možné recesi, přesto prezident odmítl nazvat situaci 'krizí'. Putin vypadal klidně a sebejistě, když vstoupil do sálu. Detailní záběry jeho obličeje se promítaly na velkých obrazovkách, které zachycovaly každý jeho výraz a gesto. Hlavním cílem Putina bylo ujistit občany, že Rusko dokáže překonat to, co nazval 'nepříznivým scénářem', a slíbil zlepšení do dvou let, možná i dříve. Za hospodářskou situaci Ruska se přímo neomluvil. Místo toho Putin pouze připustil, že Ruská centrální banka a vláda mohly reagovat na hospodářské výzvy rychleji. Hospodářské potíže Ruska přisoudil 'vnějším' faktorům a tvrdil, že sankce představují pouze '25 až 30 %' problémů. Když se reportér BBC zeptal na 'novou' studenou válku, Putin se naklonil dopředu s důrazem a prohlásil, že Rusko pouze chrání své vlastní zájmy. Poznamenal, že Moskva má v zahraničí jen dvě vojenské základny, zatímco USA mají základny 'po celém světě'. Stěžoval si, že sliby ohledně nerozšiřování NATO byly porušeny a Západ nyní staví kolem Ruska 'virtuální zdi'. Putin umí obratně přesouvat pozornost. Když byl dotázán na údajné represe čečenských úřadů vůči rodinám podezřelých teroristů a na obvinění, že ruské státem financované televizní kanály podněcují nenávist, Putin okamžitě poukázal na nedávno zveřejněnou zprávu Bílého domu o mučení. Tvrdil, že USA 'legalizovaly mučení' a dokonce vyvinuly metody, jak ho provádět, a zeptal se: 'Jak to vysvětlíte?' Putin se podrobněji vyjádřil k obrazu ruského 'medvěda' a tvrdil, že se ho Západ snaží 'spoutat' a 'zbavit drápů', místo aby mu umožnil pokojně existovat. Potenciálně pozitivní bylo Putinovo prohlášení, že konflikt na východní Ukrajině by měl být vyřešen mírovou cestou. Přiznal, že na východní Ukrajině jsou Rusové, a označil je za 'dobrovolníky'. Překvapivě Putin vyzval novináře, kteří jsou známí svým kritickým postojem ke Kremlu, což vedlo k nepříjemným otázkám. Když Putin naznačil 'tenkou hranici' mezi opozicí a 'pátou kolonou' – zrádci Ruska – novináři ho nutili, aby jmenoval členy 'páté kolony', což neudělal. Ostatní se ho ptali na plat Igora Sečina, šéfa společnosti Rosněfť, o kterém tvrdil, že ho nezná. V jednom pozoruhodném okamžiku se ruský reportér zeptal, zda se Putin obává 'palácového převratu' ze strany jeho nejbližších. Putin, který je navzdory svému drsnému image známý smyslem pro humor, odpověděl s úsměvem: 'Palácový převrat nemůžeme mít, protože žádné paláce nemáme.' Prohlásil, že stabilita závisí na podpoře ruského lidu, který 'věří, že jednáme v jeho zájmu.'

article_content: By Ruth Styles and Martha Cliff. Tyger Drew-Honey, the former child star turned documentary maker, is now exploring the reasons behind the growing pressure on modern men to look good. In the latest episode of his BBC3 series, 'Tyger Takes On...', Drew-Honey, 18, interviews boys and men who are going to extreme lengths to achieve the perfect body, including undergoing surgery and using steroids. 'I met a guy named Marcus who had taken so many steroids that he suffered a heart attack at just 18,' Drew-Honey revealed, expressing his shock. The documentary series explores male body image. 'He didn’t want to show us his body because he was ashamed, but I saw photos of him on Instagram later and he was ripped.' 'He had an amazing physique, and it seemed crazy that he felt something was wrong with it.' Insecurities about muscle mass aren't the only issues plaguing British men. According to the eating disorders charity Beat, males account for 10 to 25 per cent of anorexia and bulimia cases. So, why are men resorting to extreme measures to look good? Drew-Honey believes natural competitiveness plays a significant role. 'It’s about being competitive,' the 18-year-old star explained. 'We see images of underwear models and other pictures on Instagram, because we communicate visually these days.' Many men are overusing steroids in their pursuit of a bodybuilder physique. Men's bodies are facing similar levels of scrutiny as women's. 'We are all in a race that is driving us mad. We become increasingly competitive, ultimately competing against ourselves.' The celebrity selfie culture, he adds, exacerbates the problem by projecting an unattainable ideal for most teenagers and young adults. 'People use selfie culture to promote themselves,' he said, 'and constantly feel they must live up to the perfection they see on Facebook, Twitter and Instagram.' This trend isn't solely about attracting women. 'There is the aspect of wanting to look good for the opposite sex, but men often want to impress other men,' Drew-Honey explained. 'When I was with the boys in Coventry [for the documentary], they said they didn’t care what women thought; they only cared about what other men said, not because of their sexuality, but because of their competitive nature.' Drew-Honey himself admits to insecurities about his own physique. 'I think my main insecurities are about my body,' he confessed. 'My body is alright; I watch my diet and try to avoid eating too much, but I enjoy the occasional piece of chocolate. I don't exercise excessively, though I do walk my dog.' Some might dismiss these concerns as trivial, especially considering the pressures women have faced for years. Tyger (right) with some of the show's participants, from left: Mitch, Sammy, and James. However, Drew-Honey argues that this perspective misses the point. 'The focus on women’s issues was rightly addressed because of the problems caused by size zero models, which contributed to anorexia and bulimia.' 'But men’s insecurities also need attention because many guys are taking large amounts of steroids and spending excessive time at the gym.' He added: 'It would be ridiculous if any boy or girl had no insecurities. Everyone feels insecure at times, and I don’t think anyone is ever completely satisfied with their appearance.' 'Tyger Takes On...The Perfect Body' airs Thursday night at 9pm on BBC3.

V nejnovější epizodě své série na BBC3, 'Tyger Takes On...', Drew-Honey (18) zpovídá mladíky a muže, kteří se uchylují k extrémům, aby dosáhli dokonalého těla, včetně operací a steroidů. 'Potkal jsem kluka, Marcuse, který bral tolik steroidů, že v 18 letech prodělal infarkt,' šokovaně prozradil Drew-Honey. Tento dokument zkoumá vnímání mužského těla a ideálů krásy. 'Nechtěl nám ukázat tělo, protože se styděl, ale viděl jsem ho na Instagramu a byl fakt vypracovaný.' 'Měl skvělou postavu a bylo mi divné, že se mu na ní něco nelíbilo.' Nejistota ohledně svalů není jediný problém britských mužů. Podle organizace Beat, která se věnuje poruchám příjmu potravy, tvoří muži 10–25 % případů anorexie a bulimie. Proč se ale muži tak honí za dokonalým vzhledem? Drew-Honey věří, že velkou roli hraje soutěživost. 'Jde o to být nejlepší,' vysvětluje osmnáctiletý Drew-Honey. 'Vidíme fotky modelek a modelů spodního prádla na Instagramu, protože dnes komunikujeme hlavně vizuálně.' Mnoho mužů ve snaze o kulturistickou postavu nadužívá steroidy. Mužské tělo je zkoumáno stejně kriticky jako to ženské. 'Jsme v závodě, který nás ničí. Jsme čím dál tím víc soutěživí, až soutěžíme sami se sebou.' Kult celebrit a selfie podle něj situaci zhoršuje, protože ukazuje nereálný ideál, kterého většina teenagerů a mladých nedosáhne. 'Lidé používají selfie jako reklamu,' říká Drew-Honey, 'a mají pocit, že musí vypadat perfektně jako na Facebooku, Twitteru a Instagramu.' Nejde ale jen o to, zaujmout ženy. 'Kromě snahy líbit se opačnému pohlaví chtějí muži zapůsobit i na ostatní muže,' vysvětluje Drew-Honey. 'Když jsem natáčel s kluky v Coventry, říkali, že jim je jedno, co si myslí holky, záleží jim jen na názoru ostatních chlapů, a to ne kvůli homosexualitě, ale kvůli soutěživosti.' Sám Drew-Honey přiznává, že má komplexy ze svého těla. 'Nejvíc se asi trápím kvůli postavě,' svěřuje se. 'Jinak se snažím jíst zdravě a nepřejídat se, ale občas si dám čokoládu. Necvičím moc, ale chodím se psem.' Někdo by to mohl brát jako malichernost, obzvlášť když si uvědomíme, jaký tlak je vyvíjen na ženy. Tyger (vpravo) a někteří účinkující, zleva Mitch, Sammy a James. Drew-Honey ale nesouhlasí. 'Problémy žen se řeší právem, protože modelky s velikostí 0 způsobily anorexii a bulimii.' 'Ale i nejistoty mužů si zaslouží pozornost, protože spousta chlapů bere steroidy a tráví hodiny v posilovně.' Dodává: 'Bylo by divné, kdyby někdo neměl žádné komplexy. Každý se občas cítí nejistě a myslím, že nikdo není se sebou stoprocentně spokojený.' 'Tyger Takes On...The Perfect Body' uvidíte ve čtvrtek ve 21:00 na BBC3.

article_content: HYDERABAD: On Saturday, K Laxman, the Bharatiya Janata Party OBC Morcha National President, discussed the BJP's manifesto for the 2023 Telangana assembly elections. He asserted that public trust in the manifesto stems from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's endorsement. Laxman noted that the manifesto, released by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, carries Prime Minister Modi's guarantee. He emphasized the substantial differences between the BJP and Congress manifestos. He stated that the public trusts the BJP manifesto due to Modi's support, pointing to the perceived failure of Congress' five guarantees in Karnataka as an example. He further stated that Congress failed to deliver on its promises in Karnataka, including employment, unemployment benefits, free travel for women, and 200 units of free electricity. 'They can't even provide electricity for more than 3-4 hours,' he added. Laxman further criticized Congress, claiming they cannot even pay their workers in Karnataka. 'It was a complete failure,' he stated, 'so people won't trust them with six guarantees in Telangana, as corruption is the only guarantee they can offer. Congress only brings corruption, nepotism, and appeasement, while the 25 issues under Prime Minister Modi's guarantee address the entire Telangana region,' the BJP OBC Morcha National President said. He expressed confidence that the people of Telangana fully trust the BJP's manifesto. He compared BJP and non-BJP governments, noting that when petrol and diesel prices increased, no non-BJP government stepped in to assist the public. In contrast, Uttar Pradesh reduced prices by Rs 15, and other BJP-governed states also implemented reductions of Rs 5-10. Earlier on Saturday in Hyderabad, Amit Shah launched the BJP manifesto, assuring the public that the assurances made in the manifesto are 'Prime Minister Modi's guarantee' to Telangana. 'This manifesto is Prime Minister Modi's guarantee to Telangana,' Shah said. 'Under Atal Ji's leadership, three states were formed peacefully. Congress opposed Telangana's statehood for a long time, only creating it hastily for electoral advantages. They were never truly supportive of Telangana.' Telangana will hold Assembly elections on November 30, and the vote count is scheduled for December 3, along with those of four other states holding elections. In the 2018 Assembly election, the ruling Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), formerly known as Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS), secured 88 of the 119 seats with 47.4% of the vote share. Congress finished second with 19 seats.

article_content: Anita Mills, who once weighed 382 pounds, received straightforward advice from her doctor to aid in weight loss: consume 8 ounces of food every three hours, avoid sugary drinks, never skip meals, and, most importantly, keep her efforts private. Now having shed 242 pounds, Mills attributes her success to this final rule, which enabled her to navigate the challenging phases of her journey without external scrutiny or discouragement. According to Mills, it's more rewarding to have others notice your transformation than to announce a diet and face constant judgment. This contrasts with programs like Weight Watchers, which emphasize support as a key component, and research highlighting the importance of accountability. However, some experts believe openly discussing diet plans can be counterproductive. Dr. Jon Walz, who provides this same advice to his patients, attributes the need for secrecy to societal attitudes toward obesity. He suggests that individuals tend to associate with those who share similar lifestyles, often normalizing unhealthy habits. Walz explains that people resist change, even positive transformations in loved ones, and may attempt to revert them to familiar patterns. Mills experienced this firsthand when friends began to distance themselves after her significant weight loss. She recounts being hurt by a friend's remark about preferring her heavier, underscoring the unexpected negativity that can arise. Dr. Peter Gollwitzer from New York University supports this with research showing that public declarations of intent can diminish actual effort. Gollwitzer explains that acknowledging intentions can create a premature sense of accomplishment, reducing the drive to follow through. To counter this, he suggests either maintaining secrecy or creating detailed plans that specify when, where, and how goals will be achieved. Alternatively, sharing plans with a select few who provide genuine accountability can be effective. Fitness expert Bonnie MeChelle warns against sharing plans with negative or unsupportive individuals. However, she stresses the value of accountability from the right sources, emphasizing that keeping everything secret risks losing crucial support and guidance. Ultimately, MeChelle advises remembering that weight loss should be a personal journey, driven by internal motivation rather than external pressure.

Podle Mills je uspokojivější, když si ostatní všimnou vaší proměny, než když ohlásíte dietu a čelíte neustálému posuzování. To je v rozporu s programy jako Weight Watchers, které zdůrazňují podporu jako klíčovou složku, a výzkumem, který zdůrazňuje důležitost odpovědnosti. Někteří odborníci se však domnívají, že otevřené diskutování o dietních plánech může být kontraproduktivní. Dr. Jon Walz, který dává svým pacientům stejnou radu, připisuje potřebu utajení společenským postojům k obezitě. Naznačuje, že jednotlivci mají tendenci se sdružovat s těmi, kteří sdílejí podobný životní styl, čímž často normalizují nezdravé návyky. Walz vysvětluje, že lidé se brání změnám, dokonce i pozitivním transformacím u svých blízkých, a mohou se je pokusit vrátit ke známým vzorcům. Mills to zažila na vlastní kůži, když se od ní po výrazném úbytku váhy začali přátelé distancovat. Vzpomíná, jak ji zranila poznámka kamarádky, že se jí líbila víc, když byla tlustší, což podtrhuje nečekanou negativitu, která může nastat. Dr. Peter Gollwitzer z New York University to podporuje výzkumem, který ukazuje, že veřejné prohlašování záměrů může snížit skutečné úsilí. Gollwitzer vysvětluje, že uznání záměrů může vytvořit předčasný pocit úspěchu, což snižuje motivaci k dalšímu úsilí. Proti tomu navrhuje buď zachovat utajení, nebo vytvořit podrobné plány, které specifikují, kdy, kde a jak bude cílů dosaženo. Alternativně může být účinné sdílet plány s několika vybranými, kteří poskytují skutečnou odpovědnost. Odbornice na fitness Bonnie MeChelle varuje před sdílením plánů s negativními nebo nepodporujícími jedinci. Zdůrazňuje však hodnotu odpovědnosti ze správných zdrojů a zdůrazňuje, že utajování všeho riskuje ztrátu zásadní podpory a vedení. Závěrem MeChelle radí pamatovat si, že hubnutí by mělo být osobní cestou, poháněnou vnitřní motivací spíše než vnějším tlakem.

article_content: Tory MP Brooks Newmark suggested that the benefits cap should be reduced to the post-tax equivalent of the average £26,000 salary, amounting to just over £20,000. An influential group of Tory MPs stated that no one should be allowed to claim more than £20,000 annually in benefits. Members of the Free Enterprise Group of Conservative MPs unanimously called for the reduction of the welfare cap from its current £26,000 level. MPs suggested this measure would help generate funds for middle-class tax cuts and convey a strong message that the unemployed should not have a comfortable life on benefits. Mr. Newmark stated that many hardworking individuals in his constituency question why the welfare cap allows people to receive £26,000 effectively post-tax, which is equivalent to a £35,000 pre-tax income. He added that lowering the welfare cap to a more reasonable level would enable tax cuts elsewhere and that those who are fit and able to work should receive no more than the post-tax equivalent of £26,000. Fellow Tory David Ruffley mentioned that private polling, conducted on behalf of Number 10, indicated that about 80 percent of the public supported the benefit cap but felt it was too high, suggesting a cut to £20,000. The Free Enterprise Group, which includes rising Tory stars, was founded by Education Minister Elizabeth Truss and is supported by senior figures like Treasury Minister Sajid Javid and Business Minister Matthew Hancock. The group urged George Osborne to introduce tax cuts to alleviate pressure on middle-class families and small businesses, also advocating for raising the starting point for the 40 percent tax rate to £50,000. MPs noted that the Government had sufficiently raised the personal allowance for basic rate taxpayers and should now focus on helping those with middle incomes. Tory MP Dominic Raab commented that while progress has been made in lifting the lowest paid out of tax, the middle classes have been significantly impacted. Proposals included eliminating stamp duty on homes valued under £500,000, abolishing Air Passenger Duty, and removing 'green taxes' that cost nearly £3 billion annually. The group's proposal to raise the 40 percent tax threshold from £41,450 to £50,000 highlights tensions with the Liberal Democrats, who prefer focusing on further increases in the personal tax allowance. The group sparked controversy by proposing a single VAT rate of 15 percent, which, according to Tory MP Kwasi Kwarteng, would lower prices for most goods and services currently taxed at 20 percent. However, this would also increase VAT on domestic fuel from eight percent to 15 percent and introduce VAT on currently zero-rated items like food and children’s clothes. Mr. Kwarteng argued that consumers would benefit overall despite the controversial abolition of zero-rate VAT, criticizing the reaction against the proposal to put VAT on hot pasties. Mr. Newmark, at the launch of a policy paper, cautioned against the plan, calling it politically 'toxic'. Labour criticized the proposal as 'shocking,' claiming it would increase costs for millions of families and raise average energy bills by £120 annually.

article_content: QPR manager Harry Redknapp acknowledges that QPR needs to remain in the Barclays Premier League to retain striker Charlie Austin, who is currently in excellent form. Austin has already scored seven goals in the Premier League, making him the joint top English scorer in the division. QPR is eager to persuade Austin to extend his contract, which has 18 months remaining. Redknapp believes that avoiding relegation will be the most important factor in keeping Austin. 'Do we need to stay up to keep him? Staying up will be very important,' Redknapp stated. 'He's happy here, and he wants to continue playing in the Premier League. Having experienced it, he wants to remain there. If he scores 20 goals this year, that will greatly assist us in staying up.' Austin was playing for Poole Town in the ninth tier of English football just six years ago. The 25-year-old joined Burnley after a successful period at Swindon before transferring to QPR for £4million in August 2013. 'How much is he worth now? I couldn't put a price on him; he'll soon be seeking a new contract,' Redknapp joked. Redknapp concedes that QPR must remain in the Premier League to retain Austin. Austin was playing for Poole Town in the ninth tier of English football only six years ago. 'I don't know what he's worth, but certainly more than £4m.' QPR will host Burnley on Saturday, aiming to move out of the bottom three for the first time since September. Austin will face his former club, Burnley, whose key player, Danny Ings, is also in good form, having scored three goals in his last three games. 'They both scored goals last year in the Championship,' Redknapp said. 'Ings is in the England Under-21 team; I certainly expected him to score goals this year, and Charlie has been the same, he's carried it on. If they were playing in top-tier teams that consistently create numerous chances, they would score even more goals. It's more challenging when playing for a team lower in the league; you don't get as many opportunities and must capitalize on those that arise. That's precisely what they are doing now.' article_content: Deep within a remote South Pole observatory, American scientists have spent two years eagerly awaiting a sign, proof that their search for a nearly undetectable particle wasn't futile. Their patience has paid off: they've announced a groundbreaking discovery, labeling it a 'new age of astronomy,' marking a new frontier in understanding the universe. The $270 million, US-led IceCube facility, encompassing a cubic kilometer of Antarctic ice, has successfully detected very high-energy cosmic neutrinos. These subatomic particles originate from deep space, potentially remnants of supernovae, or exploding stars. Unlike ordinary telescopes which cannot observe these elusive neutrinos, IceCube is capable of doing so, being the world's largest neutrino telescope. Neutrinos, unlike light particles (photons), rarely interact with matter because they lack electric charge and possess very little mass, making them notoriously difficult to detect. However, the IceCube facility can detect these neutrinos, which traverse the universe in vast numbers, according to FT. Crucially, neutrinos travel in perfectly straight lines from their origin, unaffected by magnetic fields or matter absorption. This makes them invaluable to astronomers as they can escape from the core of a supernova, or other cosmic phenomena, more easily than photons. Neutrinos have been previously detected, with the first observation in 1956. However, scientists have now detected the pure form of neutrinos, possessing at least one million times more energy than previously observed. These are produced in turbulent gaseous environments, remnants of supernova explosions. The IceCube observatory was strategically built in the South Pole to maximize the chances of observing these elusive cosmic neutrinos. Researchers melted holes in the ice cap, deploying 5,160 light detectors at depths ranging from 1,500 to 2,000 meters beneath the surface. Neutrino detectors are typically constructed underground to shield them from cosmic rays and other background radiation. While trillions of neutrinos pass through the observatory every second, a select few collide with an atom in the ice at the precise angle. This collision generates electrically charged particles, emitting light that is captured by the detectors. Computers then analyze the light patterns and intensity to determine the neutrino's energy and direction. Last week, the IceCube team reported in the journal Science the detection of 28 high-energy neutrinos originating from beyond our solar system over a two-year period. While this sample size is small, these neutrinos carry staggeringly high energies. Lower-energy neutrinos abundantly reach Earth from the sun and cosmic ray interactions with the upper atmosphere, but these high-energy neutrinos come from much further away. According to Prof. Francis Halzen, principal investigator of IceCube, this discovery is what they have been searching for, marking 'the dawn of a new age of astronomy.' Two of the detected neutrinos possessed more energy than a fly in flight, concentrated into a single subatomic particle. Potential sources include supernovae and matter being drawn into massive black holes. The IceCube project is managed by the University of Wisconsin–Madison, with collaborative efforts and funding from numerous global universities and research institutions. The initial detection of neutrinos in 1956 by Clyde Cowan, Frederick Reines, et al., was confirmed and published in Science, earning them the 1995 Nobel Prize. The detection of solar neutrinos and those from Supernova 1987A initiated neutrino astronomy. Supernova neutrinos typically have energies ranging from a few to several tens of MeV. However, the sites accelerating cosmic rays are expected to produce neutrinos one million times more energetic, originating from the turbulent remnants of supernova explosions. Scientists believe this type of neutrino has now been detected for the first time. Neutrinos travel in perfectly straight lines from their source, unaffected by magnetic fields or matter absorption, providing an unadulterated view of the universe.

Zařízení IceCube za 270 milionů dolarů, vedené USA, které zahrnuje krychlový kilometr antarktického ledu, úspěšně detekovalo vysokoenergetická kosmická neutrina. Tyto subatomární částice pocházejí z hlubokého vesmíru, potenciálně pozůstatky supernov nebo explodujících hvězd. Na rozdíl od běžných teleskopů, které nemohou tato nepolapitelná neutrina pozorovat, je toho IceCube schopen, protože je největším neutrinovým teleskopem na světě. Neutrina, na rozdíl od světelných částic (fotonů), zřídka interagují s hmotou, protože postrádají elektrický náboj a mají velmi malou hmotnost, což ztěžuje jejich detekci. Zařízení IceCube však dokáže tato neutrina detekovat, která podle FT procházejí vesmírem v obrovském množství. Klíčové je, že se neutrina pohybují dokonale po přímce od svého původu, aniž by byla ovlivněna magnetickými poli nebo absorpcí hmoty. Díky tomu jsou neocenitelná pro astronomy, protože mohou snadněji uniknout z jádra supernovy nebo jiných kosmických jevů než fotony. Neutrina byla detekována již dříve, přičemž první pozorování proběhlo v roce 1956. Vědci však nyní detekovali čistou formu neutrin, která má alespoň milionkrát více energie než dříve pozorovaná. Tyto vznikají v turbulentních plynných prostředích, pozůstatcích explozí supernov. Observatoř IceCube byla strategicky postavena na jižním pólu, aby se maximalizovaly šance na pozorování těchto nepolapitelných kosmických neutrin. Vědci roztavili otvory v ledové čepici a umístili 5 160 detektorů světla do hloubek od 1 500 do 2 000 metrů pod povrchem. Neutrinové detektory se obvykle staví pod zemí, aby byly chráněny před kosmickým zářením a jiným zářením pozadí. Zatímco observatoří projdou každou sekundu biliony neutrin, jen velmi málo se srazí s atomem v ledu v přesném úhlu. Tato srážka generuje elektricky nabité částice, které vyzařují světlo, jež je zachyceno detektory. Počítače poté analyzují světelné vzorce a intenzitu, aby určily energii a směr neutrina. Minulý týden tým IceCube oznámil v časopise Science detekci 28 vysokoenergetických neutrin pocházejících z oblastí mimo naši sluneční soustavu za období dvou let. I když je tento vzorek malý, tato neutrina nesou ohromně vysoké energie. Nízkoenergetická neutrina hojně dopadají na Zemi ze slunce a interakcí kosmického záření s horní atmosférou, ale tato vysokoenergetická neutrina pocházejí z mnohem větší vzdálenosti. Podle profesora Francise Halzena, hlavního výzkumníka IceCube, je tento objev to, co hledali, a znamená 'úsvit nového věku astronomie'. Dvě z detekovaných neutrin měla více energie než moucha za letu, koncentrovanou do jediné subatomární částice. Mezi potenciální zdroje patří supernovy a hmota vtahovaná do masivních černých děr. Projekt IceCube je řízen University of Wisconsin–Madison, s úsilím o spolupráci a financováním od mnoha globálních univerzit a výzkumných institucí. Počáteční detekce neutrin v roce 1956 Clyde Cowanem, Frederickem Reinesem a dalšími byla potvrzena a publikována v časopise Science a vynesla jim Nobelovu cenu v roce 1995. Detekce slunečních neutrin a neutrin ze supernovy 1987A iniciovala neutrinovou astronomii. Neutrina ze supernov mají typicky energie v rozmezí od několika do desítek MeV. Očekává se však, že místa urychlující kosmické záření budou produkovat neutrina milionkrát energičtější, pocházející z turbulentních pozůstatků explozí supernov. Vědci se domnívají, že tento typ neutrina byl nyní poprvé detekován. Neutrina se pohybují dokonale po přímce od svého zdroje, aniž by byla ovlivněna magnetickými poli nebo absorpcí hmoty, což poskytuje nezkreslený pohled na vesmír.

article_content: Ghana's manager, Avram Grant, was in a jovial mood on Saturday, ahead of the Africa Nations Cup final against Ivory Coast, saying he would telephone Chelsea captain John Terry to get advice about taking penalties. Terry famously missed a penalty which could have won Chelsea, then managed by Grant, the 2008 Champions League final against Manchester United. The defender slipped and his shot hit the post, giving United a lifeline, allowing them to lift the trophy in Moscow. John Terry missed a crucial penalty in the 2008 Champions League final shootout against Manchester United. The Chelsea captain's missed penalty in the shootout allowed United to win 6-5. Terry remembers the 2008 miss in Moscow as one of the darkest moments of his career. Ghana's manager Avram Grant, who managed Chelsea in 2008, has taken a light-hearted view of the miss. 'I'm going to call John Terry for some advice,' Grant quipped to reporters on Saturday when asked about the possibility of the Nations Cup final being decided by penalties. The loss to Premier League rivals United was Grant's second defeat in a major final in 2008, following Tottenham Hotspur's 2-1 win over Chelsea after extra time in the League Cup final. Grant predicted a high-quality Africa Nations Cup final on Sunday when his side plays neighbours Ivory Coast in one of the continent's oldest rivalries. 'We have seen quality players and quality football throughout this tournament, but we can expect even more. There are a lot of good players in both line-ups, and I think because of that, we can expect a quality final,' Grant told reporters on Saturday. Grant said his team had been given little chance before the tournament, but improved dramatically over the three weeks of competition. 'We've shown a lot of motivation up to now, and we'll show a lot in the final.' Ghana eased past tournament hosts Equatorial Guinea in the semi-finals 3-0. Ghana and Lorient forward Jordan Ayew scored a penalty to give his side the lead against Equatorial Guinea. Ghana and Everton winger Christian Atsu takes on Equatorial Guinea defender Reuban Belima. Ghana are through to the Africa Cup of Nations final and will face rivals Ivory Coast on Sunday, February 9.

article_content: Darron Gibson is eager to prove he's fit for the upcoming match against Germany, the current World champions, as he continues his return from a significant injury. The 26-year-old recently played for Ireland, marking his first appearance in over ten months during their 2-0 victory against Oman after recovering from a cruciate ligament injury. Having played a full game for Everton in their 1-1 Europa League draw against Krasnodar, and with James McCarthy absent due to injury, Gibson aims to be selected for Saturday's Euro 2016 qualifier against Gibraltar in Dublin. He is also eyeing the subsequent challenging game against Germany. Gibson aims to put his injury struggles behind him as he vies for a spot in the Republic of Ireland squad for their Euro 2016 qualifying matches against both Gibraltar and Germany. After a cruciate ligament injury sustained in October 2013 during Ireland's World Cup qualifier against Kazakhstan sidelined him for ten months, Gibson is now feeling ready. 'I played in the European game last week and felt strong,' he said, 'so hopefully I'll get a chance to play and make an impact on Tuesday.' 'Playing against some of the best players is something every player enjoys,' Gibson added. 'It's a good test to see how you measure up.' 'Initially, it was just about getting playing time,' he explained. 'Now, I feel match-fit and ready to perform properly.' He added, 'It's been alright, although frustrating not playing in the Premier League. However, with two games in the last couple of weeks, I'm feeling good heading into this week.' Ireland is set to face Gibraltar, who previously lost 7-0 to Poland, at the Aviva Stadium. They recognize the importance of goal difference but aren't underestimating their opponent. Gibson's comeback included playing for Everton in their 1-1 draw against Krasnodar in the Europa League. Martin O'Neill hopes to secure at least four points from the upcoming double-header. Gibson emphasized, 'No game is easy. We're taking the game seriously and aiming for a win. We aren't expecting an easy victory, but we'll give it our best shot.' 'We're approaching both games with the same focus. First, we're concentrating on Saturday's game to get the result we need, then we'll move on to Germany on Tuesday.' Ireland commenced preparations in Malahide, with attention largely focused on Roy Keane's updated autobiography. O'Neill insisted this wouldn't distract the team. The lead-up to the qualifiers has been dominated by discussions surrounding Roy Keane's book. O'Neill commented, 'Our games are the priority, especially Saturday's match against Gibraltar. Building on our win against Georgia is crucial.' 'I'm not fully aware of the book's content, but its release was bound to create attention. However, the games are what matter most to us.'
