article_content: I got the sailors to lash me to the mast to observe it. I was lashed for four hours and I did not expect to escape, but I felt bound to record it if I did.' Joseph Mallord William Turner had a truly obsessional attention to art, so following in his footsteps is no easy task. British artist Andy Parker admits he will draw the line at being tied to a mast for hours on end, but nonetheless he plans to retrace the movements at sea of arguably the greatest maritime artist of all time. Parker may be relieved to know that the quote attributed to Turner by John Ruskin after his 1842 painting 'Snow Storm -- Steam-Boat off a Harbor's Mouth making Signals in Shallow Water, and going for the Lead' -- is now thought to have been apocryphal. After all, Ruskin described Turner as 'at once the painter and poet of the day,' using poetic license in the 24,000 works of art he created, of which more than 60% were water-themed. 'His style of painting, I believe, was not necessarily what's in front of you but what you want to see,' explains Parker. 'These fabulous sunsets of his were not necessarily what he saw; he could just come up with a good idea.' 'That's what makes him such a great artist, while I'm just a painter. So, I'm not trying to emulate his style but the position where he was.' Following in Turner's footsteps has been done before -- UK-born American artist Edward Moran's infatuation was such that he traveled from the United States to study his work and retrace some of the spots where he painted. Parker, however, is the first to do so for more than 150 years. The link between Parker and Turner is more than just an admiration of his work -- both were born in London's Covent Garden and were shopkeepers' sons. 'Turner's father was a barber and I'm sure the Parkers and Turners probably knew each other,' says Parker, whose family ran a saddlery business. Parker's 'big undertaking' is to visit 12 to 15 locations from Deal in Kent to Poole in Dorset, along Britain's southern coast. The amount of materials and canvases he would have to carry means he may not be able to do the whole trip at once. And while Turner set off to sea to sketch, Parker will travel the 1,000 or so miles to the various ports and harbors. But like Turner, he too plans to take to the waters and is looking for yachting enthusiasts across the country to help him in his quest. 'Chartering boats is so expensive, so I've contacted some yachting magazines to see if I can get any helpers,' he says. 'I don't want to go out for eight hours on some fishing jolly -- no one wants an artist spoiling the view. I'm just looking for a couple of hours where I can work quickly -- Turner's journeys were usually brief -- and throw down some ideas.' Parker, 56, spent the majority of his life working in the music industry before coming to painting as a profession. While Parker is 'not really a sailor,' Turner had sea legs. 'Turner was a great traveler,' says Christine Riding, head of art at London's Royal Museums Greenwich. 'He liked to travel alone or with intimate friends, who paint the picture of a mariner.' 'They paint a nice picture of him not being bothered by the stormy weather; while everyone was being sick, he carried on sketching.' 'He was a workaholic that certainly enjoyed the dynamics of the sea, and he had a very good grasp of maritime terminology. The sea was constantly imbibed in his DNA as an artist.' The Greenwich National Maritime Museum recently hosted an exhibition called 'Turner and the Sea,' the first to solely focus on his apparent obsession. 'Whether the story of him being tied to the mast or not is true, it doesn't really matter; it's just a very romantic idea,' explains Riding. 'If you take that painting, the title itself is very important. The boat's name is Aerial, and there is no evidence of a ship by that name then.' 'Turner was known to be a very poetic artist, so you think of Ariel in the Tempest, or else Ariel, the ship on which Percy Bysshe Shelley died.' At the time, the British Empire ruled the waves with the world's biggest navy. 'That was basically part of the national identity,' Riding explains. 'He's an artist responding to his history. Landscape artists by their very nature tend to have a maritime period, but it was such a key time.' 'He was born in 1775, when Captain Cook had just come back from his second voyage of discovery, and the nation was a global sea power. It was almost part of his DNA from the outset.' Riding says Parker's expedition has echoes of Moran's journey, which came shortly after Turner's death in 1851 at the age of 76. 'He traveled the south coast to emulate his artistic idol, and you can see a heavy Turner influence in his work,' Riding says. Moran's subsequent work, paintings such as 'The Shipwreck,' were very Turner-esque in their use of bold colors and glowing, turbulent skies, as boats were tossed in different directions amid stormy seas. More than a century and a half after Moran's voyage, Parker is following suit. See: The best sailing images of 2013.
translated_content: 'Nechal jsem se námořníky přivázat ke stěžni, abych to pozoroval. Byl jsem přivázaný čtyři hodiny a neočekával jsem, že uniknu, ale cítil jsem se povinen to zaznamenat, pokud se mi to podaří.' Joseph Mallord William Turner měl skutečně obsedantní zájem o umění, takže jít v jeho stopách není snadný úkol. Britský umělec Andy Parker přiznává, že se nenechá přivázat ke stěžni na dlouhé hodiny, ale přesto plánuje zmapovat námořní cesty pravděpodobně největšího námořního umělce všech dob. Parkerovi se možná uleví, když zjistí, že citát, který Turnerovi přisuzoval John Ruskin po jeho obraze z roku 1842 'Sněžná bouře – parník u ústí přístavu signalizuje v mělké vodě a jde na olovo' – je nyní považován za apokryfní. Koneckonců, Ruskin popsal Turnera jako 'zároveň malíře a básníka své doby' a použil poetickou licenci ve 24 000 uměleckých dílech, které vytvořil, z nichž více než 60 % se týkalo vody. 'Jeho styl malování, věřím, nebyl nutně o tom, co je před vámi, ale o tom, co chcete vidět,' vysvětluje Parker. 'Tyhle báječné západy slunce, které maloval, nebyly nutně to, co viděl; mohl prostě přijít s dobrým nápadem.' 'To z něj dělá tak skvělého umělce, zatímco já jsem jen malíř. Takže se nesnažím napodobovat jeho styl, ale místa, kde tvořil.' Jít v Turnerových stopách už se stalo dříve – americký umělec britského původu Edward Moran byl natolik posedlý, že cestoval ze Spojených států, aby studoval jeho dílo a zmapoval některá místa, kde maloval. Parker je však první, kdo tak činí po více než 150 letech. Spojení mezi Parkerem a Turnerem je víc než jen obdiv k jeho dílu – oba se narodili v londýnské čtvrti Covent Garden a byli syny obchodníků. 'Turnerův otec byl holič a jsem si jistý, že se Parkerovi a Turnerovi pravděpodobně znali,' říká Parker, jehož rodina provozovala sedlářskou firmu. Parkerův 'velký podnik' spočívá v návštěvě 12 až 15 míst od Deal v Kentu po Poole v Dorsetu, podél jižního pobřeží Británie. Množství materiálu a pláten, které by musel nosit, znamená, že nemusí být schopen absolvovat celou cestu najednou. A zatímco Turner se vydal na moře, aby skicoval, Parker urazí asi 1 000 mil do různých přístavů. Ale stejně jako Turner i on plánuje vyrazit na vodu a hledá jachtařské nadšence po celé zemi, kteří by mu pomohli v jeho úsilí. 'Pronájem lodí je tak drahý, a tak jsem kontaktoval některé jachtařské časopisy, abych zjistil, jestli bych mohl získat nějaké pomocníky,' říká. 'Nechci se plavit osm hodin na nějaké rybářské výpravě – nikdo nechce, aby mu umělec kazil výhled. Hledám jen pár hodin, kdy můžu rychle pracovat – Turnerovy cesty byly obvykle krátké – a hodit na papír nějaké nápady.' Parkerovi, kterému je 56 let, strávil většinu života prací v hudebním průmyslu, než se stal malířem. Zatímco Parker 'není tak úplně námořník,' Turner měl mořské nohy. 'Turner byl velký cestovatel,' říká Christine Ridingová, vedoucí umění v londýnských Royal Museums Greenwich. 'Rád cestoval sám nebo s blízkými přáteli, kteří ztvárňovali námořníky.' 'Malují si ho jako člověka, kterého netrápí bouřlivé počasí; zatímco všem bylo špatně, on dál skicoval.' 'Byl to workoholik, který si jistě užíval dynamiku moře a měl velmi dobré znalosti námořní terminologie. Moře měl jako umělec neustále v krvi.' Greenwich National Maritime Museum nedávno uspořádalo výstavu s názvem 'Turner a moře', první, která se zaměřila výhradně na jeho zjevnou posedlost. 'Ať už je příběh o tom, že byl přivázaný ke stěžni, pravdivý, nebo ne, na tom vlastně nezáleží; je to jen velmi romantická představa,' vysvětluje Ridingová. 'Pokud vezmete ten obraz, samotný název je velmi důležitý. Jméno lodi je Aerial a neexistuje žádný důkaz o lodi s tímto jménem.' 'Turner byl známý jako velmi poetický umělec, takže si vzpomenete na Ariela z Bouře od Shakespeara, nebo na Ariel, loď, na které zemřel Percy Bysshe Shelley.' V té době Britské impérium ovládalo moře díky největšímu námořnictvu na světě. 'To bylo v podstatě součástí národní identity,' vysvětluje Ridingová. 'Je to umělec, který reaguje na svou historii. Krajináři mají ze své podstaty tendenci se v určitém období věnovat námořním motivům, ale tehdy to byla obzvlášť důležitá doba.' 'Narodil se v roce 1775, kdy se kapitán Cook právě vrátil ze své druhé objevitelské plavby a národ byl globální námořní mocností. Bylo to téměř součástí jeho DNA od začátku.' Ridingová říká, že Parkerova expedice připomíná Moranovu cestu, která se uskutečnila krátce po Turnerově smrti v roce 1851 ve věku 76 let. 'Cestoval po jižním pobřeží, aby napodobil svého uměleckého idola, a v jeho díle je silně patrný Turnerův vliv,' říká Ridingová. Moranovy pozdější práce, obrazy jako 'Ztroskotání lodi', byly velmi turnerovské ve svém použití výrazných barev a zářivých, bouřlivých oblak, a lodě se zmítaly různými směry uprostřed bouřlivého moře. Více než sto padesát let po Moranově plavbě se Parker vydává v jeho stopách. Viz: Nejlepší snímky plachtění roku 2013.

article_content: By James Gordon An elderly man from Utah has been ordered to serve at least 15 years in prison for the murder of his wife in 2011. Charles Edward Dodd, 78, pleaded 'guilty but mentally ill' to one count of murder. Dodd admitted to stabbing his tenth wife, Mary W. Ratliffe, three times in the heart in August 2011. After killing her, he took a large amount of prescription drugs and drank a tumbler of vodka before stabbing himself in the chest and losing consciousness. Jailed: Charles Edward Dodd, 78, (pictured at an earlier court hearing) has been found guilty of first-degree murder in the death of his ill wife. He tried to commit suicide after killing her. He has now been sentenced to a minimum of 15 years in jail. Wife number ten: Mary W. Ratliffe is shown in the photo her family submitted for her obituary. Ratliffe, 82, was stabbed to death on August 13, 2011. Her husband, Charles Edward Dodd, has been found guilty of murder. Off to prison: Charles Edward Dodd has been sentenced to serve at least 15 years in prison for the 2011 murder of his wife. Investigators learned of Ratliffe's death and Dodd's suicide attempt after an acquaintance notified them that Dodd had left two envelopes at her office containing $7,000 in cash and two notes indicating that he intended to kill his wife and himself. 'In the note, he wrote that he didn't want Mary taken from him,' Ratliffe's daughter, Connie Pearson, told KSL news. She described him as 'anxious and worried about every little thing' in the months before the murder. The killing happened before the couple were due to move to Houston. They were a couple for 20 years and had been married for 10. Both had health problems, according to Pearson. He suffered from a condition that left his lips blue from a lack of oxygen. She had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Despite her medical condition, Pearson said her mother was healthy and active. She dismissed Dodd's claims to detectives that her mother was an invalid who wanted to die. 'This wasn't a mercy killing. This was murder,' she said. Issues over Dodd's competency to stand trial led to several delays in the case. It was no mercy killing: Mary W. Ratliffe's daughter has been critical of the way the case was handled by the Duchesne County Attorney's Office. Her primary complaints center on the length of time it took to reach a resolution in the case and a lack of communication from prosecutors. He was committed to the Utah State Hospital for at least a year and underwent three separate psychological examinations. When Dodd woke up in his hospital bed shortly after the murder, he said he wanted to 'plead guilty to the charge straight up, be sent to the (state prison) and have them put a bullet in his head,' defense attorney Bill Morrison said. As a result of that statement, the medical examiner found Dodd incompetent to stand trial. Pearson said she had hoped that Dodd would have been eligible for the death penalty. However, given his age and the 15-to-life sentence he received, she said that he will likely die behind bars. 'I'm still going through the various levels of grief,' Pearson said. 'Right now, I can't forgive him. (My mother) was an inspiration to me.' Dodd will begin serving his sentence at the state hospital before being moved to the state prison.

article_content: A unique and tender letter showcasing the bond between President Theodore Roosevelt and his youngest son, Quentin, has been put up for sale by a dealer who acquired it from a friend of the Roosevelt family. Roosevelt penned this letter to his 6-year-old son, Quentin, while visiting Yellowstone National Park in 1903. It's the only known letter from that trip to his family that has surfaced on the market. Its existence was previously unknown to scholars and institutions until it was discovered in the hands of a family friend, according to Nathan Raab, vice president of the Raab Collection, which is offering the letter for sale on its website. Raab noted, 'The relationship between Theodore Roosevelt and Quentin, his cherished son, is not widely known. Discovering a letter like this to Quentin is an extraordinary find, made even more touching by the fact that it has never been published.' The letter is valued at $25,000. In the letter, Roosevelt addresses his son affectionately as 'Quenty-Quee' and shares a brief glimpse of his experiences on the trail, including a small sketch of the mule that carried his equipment during the trip. 'I love you very much. Here is a picture of the mule that carries, among other things, my bag of clothes. There are about twenty mules in the pack train. They all follow one another in single file up and down mountain paths and across streams.' The letter closes with 'Your loving father.' Raab said, 'This letter reveals another facet of Theodore Roosevelt, who, despite being known as a 'rough rider' and a man's man, possessed a warm, affectionate relationship with his son, who inherited many of his father's physical and intellectual traits. Quentin was the apple of Theodore Roosevelt's eye.' Quentin Roosevelt, the youngest of Theodore and Edith Roosevelt's six children, was three years old when his father became president. He was known for his lively antics in the White House and later for his academic achievements, often drawing comparisons to his father. Influenced by his father's strong support for the war, he joined the United States Army Air Service and served as a fighter pilot during World War I. He tragically died in aerial combat over France at the age of 20. Raab noted that Quentin's death deeply affected the president, 'His friends said he was never the same man again, and you see the love he had for his son in this letter.'

Roosevelt napsal tento dopis svému šestiletému synovi Quentinovi během návštěvy Yellowstonského národního parku v roce 1903. Je to jediný známý dopis z této cesty, který adresoval své rodině a který se dostal na trh. Až do objevu u rodinného přítele byla jeho existence neznámá vědcům i institucím. Raab poznamenal: 'Vztah mezi Theodorem Rooseveltem a Quentinem, jeho milovaným synem, není příliš známý. Byl známý svými rošťárnami v Bílém domě a později pro své akademické úspěchy, přičemž byl často srovnáván se svým otcem. Pod vlivem otcovy silné podpory války vstoupil do Letecké služby armády Spojených států a sloužil jako stíhací pilot během první světové války. Tragicky zahynul v leteckém souboji nad Francií ve věku 20 let. Raab poznamenal, že Quentinova smrt prezidenta hluboce zasáhla: 'Jeho přátelé říkali, že už nikdy nebyl stejný, a v tomto dopise je vidět láska, kterou ke svému synovi choval.'

article_content: Dr. Mohammed Naiyer, a general practitioner from the NSW North Coast, has been found guilty of professional misconduct by the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal. The charges stem from inappropriate behavior towards two female patients in 2011. According to reports, Dr. Naiyer's actions included 'nuzzling' a 25-year-old woman's breast, identified as Patient A, while conducting a skin examination during a mole removal follow-up. This occurred after a nurse, who was present during the removal procedure, had left the room. Patient A stated that she saw Dr. Naiyer's mouth brushing or nuzzling her breast during the examination. The incident took place at the medical center where Dr. Naiyer practiced. In a separate incident earlier that year, Patient A visited the center with concerns about a possible STI. During this visit, Dr. Naiyer used a dermascope to examine a mole on her breast, and Patient A reported feeling his head moving in a circular motion over her breast. Furthermore, after taking blood samples, Dr. Naiyer performed a physical examination, including internal and external examinations of her vagina and anus. The tribunal found this examination unnecessary and noted that Dr. Naiyer did not record the details, despite it being legally required. He later denied the examination took place and was found to have provided false information to the Health Care Complaints Commission. A second patient, Patient B, a 32-year-old woman, testified against Dr. Naiyer, stating that he used a dermascope to examine a mole on her breast while moving his head in a circular motion. Patient B also reported that Dr. Naiyer asked her to save his mobile number and suggested meeting for coffee. During the proceedings, Dr. Peter Kean Mun Lye, a skin cancer primary care physician, testified that in his 22 years of experience, he never needed any part of his face to touch a patient while using a dermascope. Dr. Hein Carel Vandenbergh, a NSW skin cancer practitioner and GP, also testified that a direct vaginal examination for an STI requires a swab or speculum. A further hearing on this matter is scheduled for May 28. The article's comment section is currently disabled.

article_content: Say goodbye to the Share button, as the Like button is evolving to take its place. After months of updates, Facebook has released a change that fundamentally alters the Like button's functionality, making it similar to a Share button. Now, clicking the Like button will post a full story, including a headline, blurb, and thumbnail, to your profile wall. You'll also have the option to comment on the story link. Previously, only a simple link would appear in the recent activity feed, often unnoticed. Users may now be more cautious about clicking the Like button, considering its prominent display on their walls and in their networks' newsfeeds, which should ultimately increase traffic to publishers' websites. Facebook has been gradually updating its Like button and has slowed development on the Share Button. Facebook Spokeswoman Malorie Lucich stated that while the company will continue to support the Share button, the Like button is the 'recommended solution moving forward.' However, Lucich later described it as a test, saying, 'We're always testing new products incorporating developer feedback to improve the Platform experience, and have no further details to share at this time.' It's unlikely that the change is just a test; typically, such tests from Facebook affect only a small subset of users, whereas this change affects all Like buttons. Perhaps the change was necessary because it was never clearly communicated to users that the Like button would function differently from the Share button. Many users never fully understood what it meant to click 'Like' on content. Making the result similar to the Share button could build stronger user expectations, ultimately creating a better user experience. © 2013 MASHABLE.com. All rights reserved.

article_content: A new study indicates that resveratrol, a component found in red wine, might lead to abnormal pancreatic development in unborn babies if consumed during pregnancy. Researchers advise pregnant women to avoid red wine, even in small amounts, suggesting that a seemingly beneficial ingredient could potentially harm the fetal pancreas. Resveratrol, often celebrated for its protective qualities against ailments like heart disease, cancer, and Alzheimer's, is naturally present in red wine, red grapes, and certain berries. It is also available as a dietary supplement. However, recent research suggests that it may contribute to developmental issues in the fetal pancreas. The research was conducted by the Division of Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism along with the Division of Reproductive and Development Science at Oregon Health and Science University in the United States. Dr. Kevin Gove, the lead researcher, emphasized the study's relevance to human health. Dr. Gove stated, 'This research has direct implications for human health. Resveratrol is widely recognized for its health advantages and is easily accessible over the counter. The crucial takeaway from this study is that pregnant women need to be extremely mindful of their consumption habits and should refrain from taking supplements like resveratrol without consulting their healthcare providers. What benefits the mother might not necessarily benefit the baby.' In the study, Dr. Grove and his team administered resveratrol supplements daily throughout pregnancy to obese macaque monkeys who were on a Western diet. A separate group of obese monkeys did not receive the supplement. Both groups were compared to lean monkeys who were fed a healthy diet. The animals were closely monitored for health problems, and ultrasound was used to assess blood flow through the placenta. The study, conducted on monkeys at Oregon Health and Science University in the U.S., concluded that resveratrol consumption during pregnancy has 'a direct relevance to human health.' Analyses of the fetuses showed clear evidence of pancreatic abnormalities. The findings were published in the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology Journal. Dr. Gerald Weissmann, editor-in-chief of the journal, noted, 'We've known for quite some time that resveratrol is pharmacologically active, and we're only now beginning to fully grasp the advantages and disadvantages of consuming high concentrations of this substance. As we establish a safety profile for resveratrol and other dietary supplements, results such as these shouldn't surprise us. There are always potential negative consequences when you overindulge in anything.'

Výzkumníci doporučují těhotným ženám, aby se vyhýbaly červenému vínu, a to i v malém množství, a naznačují, že zdánlivě prospěšná složka by mohla potenciálně poškodit slinivku plodu. Resveratrol, často oslavovaný pro své ochranné vlastnosti proti onemocněním jako jsou srdeční choroby, rakovina a Alzheimerova choroba, je přirozeně přítomen v červeném víně, červených hroznech a některých bobulích. Je také k dispozici jako doplněk stravy. Nicméně nedávný výzkum naznačuje, že může přispívat k vývojovým problémům ve slinivce plodu. Výzkum byl proveden Divizí diabetu, obezity a metabolismu spolu s Divizí reprodukční a vývojové vědy na Oregonské univerzitě zdraví a vědy ve Spojených státech. Dr. Kevin Gove, vedoucí výzkumník, zdůraznil význam studie pro lidské zdraví. Dr. Gove uvedl: 'Tento výzkum má přímé důsledky pro lidské zdraví. Resveratrol je široce uznáván pro své zdravotní výhody a je snadno dostupný bez lékařského předpisu. Klíčovým poznatkem z této studie je, že těhotné ženy musí být mimořádně opatrné ohledně svých stravovacích návyků a neměly by užívat doplňky stravy, jako je resveratrol, bez konzultace se svými lékaři. Co je prospěšné pro matku, nemusí být nutně prospěšné pro dítě.' Ve studii Dr. Grove a jeho tým podávali denně doplňky stravy s resveratrolem obézním makakům, kteří byli na západní stravě, po celé těhotenství. Samostatná skupina obézních opic doplněk nedostávala. Obě skupiny byly srovnávány s štíhlými opicemi, které byly krmeny zdravou stravou. Zvířata byla pečlivě sledována pro zdravotní problémy a ultrazvukem bylo hodnoceno prokrvení placenty. Studie provedená na opicích na Oregonské univerzitě zdraví a vědy v USA dospěla k závěru, že konzumace resveratrolu během těhotenství má 'přímý význam pro lidské zdraví.' Analýzy plodů prokázaly jasné důkazy o abnormalitách slinivky břišní. Zjištění byla publikována v časopise Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology Journal. Dr. Gerald Weissmann, šéfredaktor časopisu, poznamenal: 'Už nějakou dobu víme, že resveratrol je farmakologicky aktivní, a teprve nyní začínáme plně chápat výhody a nevýhody konzumace vysokých koncentrací této látky. Jakmile stanovíme bezpečnostní profil pro resveratrol a další doplňky stravy, výsledky jako tyto by nás neměly překvapit. Vždy existují potenciální negativní důsledky, když se v čemkoli přehání.'

article_content: According to Steve Hopkins, cats named Coco and dogs named Max are the most frequently rehomed at Battersea Dogs and Cats Home. Battersea Dogs and Cats Home, which cared for approximately 9,000 animals last year, has released a list of the five 'unluckiest' names based on the unwanted pets they have taken care of. The unluckiest dog names are Max, Charlie, Buster, Bailey, and Alfie, while the cat names are Coco, Tigger, Princess, Daisy, and Frankie. Cats named Coco and dogs named Max are the most likely to need rehoming. Battersea currently houses four cats named Coco and two named Tigger, along with four dogs named Buster and two named Max. Coco, a nine-year-old cat, is just one example of an animal the center must care for because her previous owner could no longer look after her. Carly Whyborn, Battersea’s head of operations, noted that certain names 'seem to be more unlucky for pets'. She explained that 'the top five names in each category are lovely but seem to be more common in our three centers in London, Brands Hatch, and Old Windsor'. Cats named Princess are also frequently taken in by the shelter. Dogs named Alfie, along with Max, Charlie, Buster, and Bailey, are most often taken in by Battersea Dogs and Cats Home. 'Battersea cares for all homeless dogs and cats, regardless of their name, and hopes animal lovers will give a second chance to all the unwanted Busters, Charlies, and Cocos out there,' the shelter stated. The shelter also revealed that the most common dog breed they took in was a Staffordshire Bull Terrier. The average age of arriving animals was one year and one month for cats, and nine months for dogs.

Nejnešťastnější psí jména jsou Max, Charlie, Buster, Bailey a Alfie, zatímco kočičí jména jsou Coco, Tigger, Princess, Daisy a Frankie. Battersea v současné době ubytovává čtyři kočky jménem Coco a dvě jménem Tigger, spolu se čtyřmi psy jménem Buster a dvěma jménem Max. Coco, devítiletá kočka, je jen jedním příkladem zvířete, o které se centrum musí starat, protože se o ni její předchozí majitel již nemohl starat. Carly Whyborn, vedoucí provozu v Battersea, poznamenala, že některá jména 'se zdají být pro mazlíčky nešťastnější'.
